intro_cards.title: About these notes
body: 8 units · tectonics to contours

Grade 12 is “geography of Eritrea in depth”. Grade 11 is the toolkit: how the crust moves, how water and wind carve, how people settle, then a first look at Eritrea’s place, relief and contour maps. Read each unit as a *story with a cause* — examiners mark the cause, not only the landform name.

intro_cards.title: Worked contour gradient
body: Two points: 1 200 m and 1 000 m. Map distance between them is 4 cm. Scale 1:50 000 (1 cm = 500 m).
Rise = 200 m. Run = 4 × 500 = 2 000 m. Gradient = 200/2000 = 1 in 10 (or 10%). Write both the fraction and a sentence: “For every 10 m walked horizontally you climb 1 m.”

units.title: Gradation by Rivers and Winds
units.intro: **Gradation** is the slow flattening of the land: high places are worn down (*degradation*) and low places are filled (*aggradation*). Agents: rivers, wind, waves (Unit 3), ice (less relevant here), and gravity (mass was

cards.title: 2.1.1 Degradation force
body: Degradation (Denudation) is the lowering of land by weathering and erosion due to the action of sun, rain, wind, rivers, frost and ice.
The change that comes on the surface of the rock due to the change of weather is called weathering.

cards.title: 2.1.2 Aggradation
body: Aggradation (Deposition) is the raising of the height of land by the deposition of the weathered and eroded materials.
After a long period of consolidation, these sediments can form sedimentary rocks.

cards.title: Gradation
body: **Gradation** is the levelling of the land surface by **degradation** (wearing down: weathering and erosion) and **aggradation** (building up by deposition). Agents: running water,

cards.title: Gradation by rivers & winds
body: Erosion, transport, deposition reshape land. Rivers: V-valleys, meanders, deltas.
Wind: deflation, dunes in arid areas.

cards.title: River profile
body: Upper: erosion dominates. Middle: transport. Lower: deposition / floodplains.
Load: dissolved, suspended, bed load.

cards.title: Gradation by Rivers and Winds: checklist before exam
body: Can you define every bold term in **Gradation by Rivers and Winds** without looking?
Can you redo each worked example with the answer covered?
Can you sketch one diagram/graph/map and label it in under 2 minutes?

cards.title: 2.2.1 What is a rRiver?
body: A river is a flow of water in a natural channel.
Most rivers begin flowing from wet mountains, springs, lakes or melting snow.

cards.title: 2.2.2 The work of a river
body: First, it erodes the land in a particular place.
Second, it deposits the eroded materials in other places.

cards.title: Common mix-ups in Gradation by Rivers and Winds
body: Write one idea students often confuse with this topic, then the correct distinction.
Example pattern: “Looks like X, but actually Y because …”
Teaching the difference is better than re-reading the page.

cards.title: 2.3.1 Upper stage
body: The upper stage of a river is usually found on mountainous areas where the slopes are steep.
The river water has high speed and few tributaries.

cards.title: 2.3.2 Middle stage
body: The rate of erosion decreases, becausethe river flows slowly along a gentle slope.
In the middle part of middle course, the valley becomes wider by lateralerosion.

cards.title: 2.3.3 Lower stage
body: In the lower Stage the river flows across a gentler slope or flat lands.
The river flows very slowly because the gradient is now very gentle or flat.
